inline_comments.comment:
This change swaps the authoritative root-level `htmlLabels` setting for the deprecated `flowchart.htmlLabels` path. According to the config schema (`config.schema.yaml`, lines 164–168), `flowchart.htmlLabels` is explicitly marked deprecated; the root-level `htmlLabels` is the correct field and takes precedence. Using `getConfig()?.flowchart?.htmlLabels` will silently ignore users who only set the recommended top-level setting.

The project already has `getEffectiveHtmlLabels(config)` in `config.ts` that correctly handles the fallback chain (`htmlLabels → flowchart.htmlLabels → true`). The line should be:
```ts
const useHtmlLabels = node.useHtmlLabels || getEffectiveHtmlLabels(getConfig());
```

`getConfig()` is called twice per image inside `setupImage()` — once for the truthiness check and once to read the value. Per the project's performance guidelines, `getConfig()` should be called once and the result cached:
```ts
const cfg = getConfig();
const bodyFontSize = cfg.fontSize
  ? cfg.fontSize
  : window.getComputedStyle(document.body).fontSize;
```

`log.debug` was changed to `log.info` here (and in the corresponding dagre-wrapper file). Per the project's logging convention, development-tracing statements like `'vertexText' + vertexText` should use `log.debug()` or `log.trace()`, not `log.info()`. `log.info` is for meaningful operational messages, not per-call shape data.
Same issue as the rendering-util copy: `log.debug` was changed to `log.info` for a verbose per-invocation trace message. This should remain `log.debug`.

The `padding-right: 1px` style that existed in the previous implementation has been silently removed (replaced with `line-height: 1.5` and `text-align: center`). The original padding comment said 'Fix for firefox'. Removing it without a note explaining why the Firefox fix is no longer needed (or that it's been superseded) makes it hard to audit visually and may cause subtle regressions on Firefox.

The added `typeof styleArray === 'string'` branch now returns the raw string instead of throwing (the old `reduce` on a plain string would have thrown). This is a silent behaviour change; the additional branch is a real bug fix but isn't mentioned in the changeset or PR description. Worth calling out explicitly so reviewers know this is intentional.

In the SVG (non-HTML) label path: `svgLabel.setAttribute('style', style.replace('color:', 'fill:'))` — if `style` is `undefined` or `null` this will throw. The null guard added for the HTML path (`style ? style.replace(...) : style`) was not applied here. The HTML path defensively handles `undefined` style now, but the SVG path is still unguarded.

The changeset bump type is `'mermaid': patch` (lowercase — correct). However, the description says 'Refactor shared label rendering logic … with no markdown-specific changes'. The PR actually adds KaTeX and icon-pack support to previously unsupported label paths and silently removes `padding-right: 1px`, changes text alignment, and modifies logging levels. Calling this a pure refactor with no functional changes is misleading; consider a `minor` bump since it adds new capabilities.

general_comments.comment: Both `packages/mermaid/src/rendering-util/rendering-elements/createLabel.js` and `packages/mermaid/src/dagre-wrapper/createLabel.js` are modified in this PR and now contain nearly identical `addHtmlLabel` implementations (same body, line-for-line). The stated goal of the PR is to reduce duplication, but instead it produces two copies of the new implementation. If the intention is for the dagre-wrapper path to eventually be removed or both to delegate to a shared utility, that should be tracked with a `// TODO:` comment referencing an issue.

The `DEFAULT_WRAPPING_WIDTH = 200` constant is duplicated at the top of both `createLabel.js` files and also inside `getWrappingWidth()`, which is itself duplicated across both files. Extracting this constant (and the helper function) into a shared module would avoid the dual-maintenance burden introduced by this PR.

In `dagre-wrapper/createLabel.js`, the FontAwesome icon replacement regex `/fa[blrs]?:fa-[\w-]+/g` is applied inline to `node.label` rather than going through `replaceIconSubstring` from `createText.js`. `replaceIconSubstring` (which was previously imported and used here) does additional work — it fetches icon SVG data from registered icon packs — so inlining a simplified regex silently loses iconpack support that `replaceIconSubstring` provides. The PR removes that import and replaces it with a regex that only handles FontAwesome class-based icons, not SVG-based icon packs.
